questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_01_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which principle is most directly associated with Magna Carta?
options: A ruler is subject to law and lawful procedure.
Citizens must elect a president.
Political parties must compete for power.
Judges may create taxes.
questions.rationale: Magna Carta became an enduring symbol that rulers are constrained by law and lawful judgment.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_02_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which development best reflects the influence of the English Bill of Rights?
options: A hereditary monarch receives unlimited authority.
Government recognizes stated protections and the executive cannot suspend laws alone.
Colonies immediately become independent republics.
Courts combine all legislative and executive power.
questions.rationale: The English Bill of Rights limited monarchical power and affirmed parliamentary authority and stated protections.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_03_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why is the Mayflower Compact evidence of consent of the governed?
options: It ended every form of monarchy.
It separated government into three branches.
Its signers agreed to form a political community and make laws for the common good.
It listed grievances against Parliament.
questions.rationale: The signers used a written agreement to create a civil political body and authorize self-government.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_04_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which statement best connects John Locke to the Declaration of Independence?
options: Both make inherent rights and consent central to legitimate government.
Both defend hereditary privilege.
Both argue that rulers create all human rights.
Both describe the exact structure of Congress.
questions.rationale: Locke and the Declaration share the reasoning that rights are inherent and legitimate government rests on consent.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_05_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which constitutional feature most clearly reflects Montesquieu’s influence?
options: A single official controls every branch.
Power is divided among legislative, executive, and judicial institutions.
Public officials inherit office.
States may ignore the Constitution.
questions.rationale: Montesquieu connected divided governmental power to preventing tyranny.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_06_Enhanced
questions.prompt: What was the primary political contribution of Thomas Paine’s Common Sense?
options: It served as the final text of the Constitution.
It persuaded a broad colonial audience to support independence and republican government.
It created the Supreme Court.
It ratified the English Bill of Rights.
questions.rationale: Common Sense was persuasive revolutionary writing that broadened support for independence; it was not a governing charter.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_07_Enhanced
questions.prompt: The Declaration states that governments derive just powers from consent. Which principle does this most directly express?
options: Popular sovereignty
Hereditary monarchy
Judicial supremacy
Executive privilege
questions.rationale: Consent means the people are the ultimate source of legitimate governmental authority.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_08_Enhanced
questions.prompt: How do the English Bill of Rights and Declaration of Independence differ most clearly?
options: Only the Declaration concerns liberty.
The English Bill of Rights limits monarchy within an existing system; the Declaration justifies separation and a new government.
The two documents have the same purpose and political result.
The Declaration grants Parliament greater authority.
questions.rationale: The documents share liberty concerns but differ in purpose, audience, and political result.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_09_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why is it inaccurate to say that an earlier source “influenced” America only if its words were copied exactly?
options: Influence can transmit a principle or reasoning that a later system adapts.
Influence always requires identical spelling.
Older sources cannot affect later institutions.
Only court decisions can influence government.
questions.rationale: Political influence often involves adapting an idea to new circumstances rather than copying exact language.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_10_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A governor takes property without notice, a hearing, or lawful authority. Which earlier tradition most directly helps challenge the action?
options: Magna Carta’s principle of lawful judgment and limits on rulers
Common Sense’s publication strategy
The Mayflower voyage route
Montesquieu’s biography
questions.rationale: The scenario centers on lawful procedure and a ruler’s subjection to law.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_11_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which sequence best represents social-contract reasoning?
options: Government creates people, then grants humanity.
People possess rights, create government by consent, and expect it to protect those rights.
A monarch owns rights and lends them to subjects.
Law exists only when every person agrees with every decision.
questions.rationale: Social-contract theory places people and rights before the government they authorize.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_12_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes popular sovereignty from a temporary majority preference?
options: Popular sovereignty means the people are the source of authority within constitutional rules.
Popular sovereignty means any majority may ignore rights.
The terms are identical in every circumstance.
Popular sovereignty eliminates representation.
questions.rationale: Popular sovereignty identifies the ultimate source of authority; constitutional procedures and rights still limit its exercise.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_13_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which item is a primary source for studying the Declaration’s political ideas?
options: A modern textbook summary
The Declaration’s 1776 text
A student’s unsourced social-media post
A fictional film made centuries later
questions.rationale: The text created in 1776 is direct evidence from the historical event and participants.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_14_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which list is in correct chronological order?
options: Declaration, Magna Carta, Mayflower Compact, English Bill of Rights
Magna Carta, Mayflower Compact, English Bill of Rights, Declaration
Mayflower Compact, Declaration, Magna Carta, English Bill of Rights
English Bill of Rights, Magna Carta, Declaration, Mayflower Compact
questions.rationale: The dates are 1215, 1620, 1689, and 1776.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_15_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A constitution gives one person the power to write laws, enforce them, and decide guilt. Which Enlightenment warning applies?
options: Locke’s defense of inherited office
Montesquieu’s warning against concentrated power
Paine’s support for monarchy
Magna Carta’s requirement for political parties
questions.rationale: Concentrating legislative, executive, and judicial authority creates the danger Montesquieu described.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_16_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why can Common Sense be influential even though it was not a law?
options: Persuasive arguments can change public opinion and political action.
Only legally binding texts influence history.
It secretly amended the Constitution.
It appointed government officials.
questions.rationale: Influence includes changing public understanding and support, not only creating enforceable law.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_17_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which evidence pair best supports the claim that Locke influenced the Declaration?
options: Locke: natural rights and consent; Declaration: inherent rights and just powers from consent
Locke: divine right; Declaration: hereditary monarchy
Locke: three branches; Declaration: judicial review
Locke: taxation; Declaration: congressional districts
questions.rationale: The shared rights-and-consent framework is the strongest intellectual connection.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_18_Enhanced
questions.prompt: What is an important limit when using the Mayflower Compact as evidence of American democracy?
options: It illustrates consent among its signers but did not create universal political equality.
It had no connection to self-government.
It immediately gave every resident equal voting rights.
It established the modern presidency.
questions.rationale: Strong historical reasoning recognizes both the document’s contribution and the limits of participation at the time.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_19_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which statement best avoids overstating Magna Carta’s influence?
options: It introduced every feature of modern U.S. democracy.
It contributed a principle of law-bound government but did not create modern American equality or institutions.
It was the first U.S. Constitution.
It abolished monarchy worldwide.
questions.rationale: Magna Carta’s enduring principle matters, but it should not be treated as a complete modern constitution.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_20_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which comparison between English legal traditions and Enlightenment thought is most accurate?
options: English traditions supplied experiences with legal limits and rights; Enlightenment thinkers supplied broader theories of rights, consent, and divided power.
They contributed exactly the same ideas in exactly the same way.
Neither affected American political thought.
English traditions addressed only geography; Enlightenment thought addressed only trade.
questions.rationale: The two streams overlapped but made distinguishable legal, institutional, and theoretical contributions.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_21_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which thesis best answers how founding influences shaped American constitutional government?
options: One document independently invented the entire system.
American constitutional ideas developed by adapting legal traditions, colonial self-government, Enlightenment reasoning, and revolutionary argument.
The Constitution rejected every earlier idea.
Only military events shaped political institutions.
questions.rationale: The strongest thesis recognizes multiple interacting influences and adaptation.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_22_Enhanced
questions.prompt: An AI tool claims that the Declaration created the three branches of government. What is the best next step?
options: Copy the claim because AI sounds confident.
Verify the Declaration’s text and compare its purpose with the Constitution before answering.
Ask AI to write the quiz response.
Ignore all primary sources.
questions.rationale: Responsible use requires checking the primary source; the Declaration states ideals and justifies independence rather than designing three branches.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_23_Enhanced
questions.prompt: What can an image of the engrossed Declaration add to analysis that a short quotation cannot?
options: Evidence of the document’s formal public presentation and physical structure
Proof that every colonist signed it
A complete description of the Constitution’s branches
Evidence that the text had no audience
questions.rationale: A document image provides visual evidence about form, presentation, and the act of making a public political statement.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_24_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A student argues that Magna Carta alone explains limited government. Which response best addresses a counterclaim?
options: Agree and ignore all other evidence.
Acknowledge Magna Carta’s importance, then explain how the English Bill of Rights and Enlightenment reasoning also strengthened limits on power.
Claim Magna Carta was written in 1776.
Replace evidence with personal preference.
questions.rationale: Good reasoning recognizes competing evidence and explains how several sources contributed.

questions.name: USG_U01_L02_Quiz_25_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A city charter divides lawmaking, enforcement, and adjudication while stating that officials must follow published procedures. Which two influence strands are most visible?
options: Montesquieu’s divided power and the English tradition of law-bound government
Paine’s independence argument and hereditary monarchy
The Mayflower voyage and royal absolutism
Natural geography and political parties
questions.rationale: The scenario combines separation of powers with the older principle that officials are subject to known law and procedure.
